correctness.rationale: An orientation of the query graph F containing an undirected cycle can realize a directed cycle, so shattering requires a forest. When two comparable poset elements lie in the same query tree, orient the unique path opposite their fixed precedence; shattering fails, so each component must be an antichain. A directed cycle of fixed poset relations among query components can be connected by suitable within-tree path orientations to obstruct at least one label pattern. Conversely, if the quotient DAG is acyclic, any orientation of forest F remains acyclic with all fixed poset relations: a hypothetical directed cycle entirely inside a component contradicts forest/antichain, and a cycle across components projects to a quotient directed closed walk. Topological sorting yields every answer pattern. Longest chains force >=height(P) forest components, giving VCdim<=n-height; antichain rank levels each with spanning tree attain equality. Empty/total/antichain cases obey the stated conventions. An independently written full n=4 oracle tested 219 distinct labeled posets times 64 supports = 14,016 cases, comparing all linear-extension traces to the quotient criterion, with zero mismatches. Infinite validity follows from the graph proof, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The no-precedence antichain case recovers the classical all-permutation forest criterion; Mirsky rank levels are classical. Those are acknowledged. Semantic searches of linear extensions, static pairwise comparisons, VC shattering and height found no earlier all-fixed-poset forest+antichain+acyclic-quotient classification. Duan–Ouyang–Wang 2024/26 study VC dimensions of compatibility sets whose instances are entire posets/total orders, not individual pairwise precedence queries within linear extensions of a fixed poset. Dittmer–Pak address counting rather than trace shattering; related SCOPE records concern different adaptive/constrained hypotheses. The new quotient-cycle obstruction is not implied merely by the known antichain forest case; best-of-knowledge PASS with terminological search risk.
